question_text: Fill in the blank: 'Neither the manager nor the employees ___ satisfied with the new policy.'

hint_ladder.title: Orient
hint_ladder.text: This sentence uses a special pairing: 'neither...nor'. When you see this structure, there's a simple rule about which noun the verb should match.

hint_ladder.title: Rule
hint_ladder.text: With 'neither...nor' (and also 'either...or'), the verb agrees with the noun that is closer to it. Think of it as the verb being polite and looking...

hint_ladder.title: Apply
hint_ladder.text: Look at the two nouns: 'the manager' and 'the employees'. Which one is right before the blank? It's 'employees'. So the verb must match 'employees'.

hint_ladder.title: Nearly Give Away
hint_ladder.text: 'Employees' is plural, so you need a plural verb in the present tense. Among the options, only one word fits that description. Which one is it?

A.text: You might have chosen A because 'manager' is singular and the first subject, but in 'neither...nor', verb agrees with nearer 'employees' ...

B.text: Correct. The plural 'are' matches the closest subject 'employees' in present tense.

C.text: You might have chosen C because 'was' is past tense singular, but the sentence needs present plural for 'employees'.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'has been' is singular, but you need plural 'have been' or simple present 'are'.

next_time_rule: For 'neither...nor' / 'either...or', the verb follows the nearest subject. Tanong mo lang: 'Sino katabi ng blank?'
deconstruct_text:
Kapag 'neither...nor' ang gamit, laging tandaan: ang verb ay sumusunod sa subject na pinakamalapit sa kanya, hindi sa unang subject. Parang sa pila, yung nasa harap ang priority.

Sa isang meeting ng barangay, pinag-usapan ang bagong curfew. 'Neither the kapitan nor the kagawads are satisfied.' Dahil 'kagawads' plural, 'are' dapat.

Mental trick: Isipin mo ang verb ay parang batang nagtatanong, 'Sino ba katabi ko?' Kung plural, plural din ang sagot. Kaya sa 'employees', 'are' ang sagot, hindi 'is'.

Subukan mong baliktarin: 'Neither the employees nor the manager is satisfied.' Ngayon 'manager' singular na ang katabi, kaya 'is' na. Practice mo 'to, sure pass!
